action: The FBI urges exchanges to block the addresses it lists for the Binance laundering. General advice: join video calls through the official app with an invite code, keep the webcam off until you verify the host, and never run scripts or paste code to fix audio.
actor: TraderTraitor (Binance theft); Sapphire Sleet / UNC1069 / BlueNoroff (FaceStealer)
exec: A large asset recovery, with a warning that the same group now targets open-source software developers through fake meeting invitations.
plain: US courts approved seizing or freezing over $1.2 billion of the more than $6 billion North Korean hackers took from Binance, and prosecutors disrupted a fake video-meeting scam used to plant malware.

key_findings: More than $6 billion in virtual assets was taken from Binance on or about October 29, 2026; the FBI attributes it to TraderTraitor, part of the North Korean military.
Courts authorised seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion; government and private efforts together have frozen more than $2.7 billion.
FaceStealer actors stole more than $400 million over 18 months from crypto and Web3 workers using hijacked accounts and staged video meetings.
The FBI seized more than 900 secretly recorded victim webcam videos; open-source maintainers are also targeted, possibly to enable supply-chain attacks.
The Central District of California disrupted cloud-based infrastructure used in the scheme; no domains or servers are named.
recommendations: Read the FBI's FaceStealer report for protective practices and post-compromise steps.
Virtual asset service providers should block transactions involving addresses TraderTraitor uses to launder the Binance assets.
Use the FBI's FaceStealer resource page if you believe you were targeted.

summary: The Justice Department said courts authorised the seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion of over $6 billion in virtual assets taken from Binance on or about October 29, 2026, which the FBI attributes to North Korea's TraderTraitor. On 23 November the department said the US filed a civil claim to forfeit over $1.1 billion of USDC. It also disrupted cloud infrastructure behind FaceStealer.

evidence.quote: the court-authorized seizure and restraint of more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency recently stolen from Binance
stole more than $6 billion worth of virtual assets from the Binance cryptocurrency exchange

the United States filed a civil claim to forfeit over $1.1 billion of USDC, a stablecoin issued by Circle Internet Financial, LLC, that is proceeds and laundered funds from the cryptocurrency theft from Binance.
